result.title: MRFlow: Mechanism-Structured Residual Flow Matching for Virtual Cell Perturbation Prediction
result.summary: Predicting cellular responses to chemical and genetic perturbations is a central test for AI virtual cells, yet many single-cell models reduce each condition to an average expression shift. This target is misaligned with perturbation biology: rare states, resistant subpopulations, and context-dependent effect sizes may coexist under the same intervention. MRFlow treats virtual-cell prediction as conditional transport between empirical single-cell measures. Control and perturbed cells are embedded in a variational latent state space, greedy low-cost supervision is constructed over detached minibatch states, and a conditional flow-matching vector field transports control populations toward perturbed populations. The field decomposes into a mechanism-structured affine dictionary, which recombines shared latent response operators with a low-rank condition-specific correction, and a spectrally controlled residual field for nonlinear cell-level variation. Genetic perturbations are encoded through a regulatory-graph GCN, chemical perturbations through Morgan fingerprints, and both enter the same conditional dynamics interface. Across eight gene and drug perturbation benchmarks, MRFlow attains the highest composite score while preserving competitive raw performance on differential-expression and distributional metrics. The results support latent distribution transport as a principled and empirically effective formulation for perturbation-aware virtual cell modeling.

AI.brief_summary: MRFlow 把虚拟细胞扰动预测重构为单细胞群体间的条件传输问题：将对照与扰动细胞嵌入变分 latent 空间，用条件 flow matching 向量场把对照群体输运到扰动群体，该向量场分解为共享 latent 响应算子构成的对角字典与低秩条件修正，再加谱控制的残差场刻画非线性细胞级变异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「latent 空间中由向量场生成并更新状态、共享算子与条件修正解耦」的做法，可能为 LVR 的推理状态生成与更新、共享与任务特定结构分配提供可核查线索，但属于单细胞生物学领域，迁移性需人工判断。
